tldr: This paper proposes an electromagnetic-guided graph learning method for fluid antenna beamforming, focusing on port placement and current-domain constraints.
motivation: To address performance degradation in compact fluid antenna arrays due to mutual coupling and uneven current loading, by jointly optimizing port placement and transmission.
method: Uses a graph neural network to predict port layouts from channel observations, refined with geometric and mutual-impedance information, and trained with a joint objective considering communication performance and electromagnetic feasibility.
result: Under a common feasibility standard, the method provides a controllable tradeoff among communication rate, current loading, and configuration latency.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively balances communication and electromagnetic constraints, offering a practical solution for fluid antenna beamforming.

title: MiLAC-Aided Beamforming For Mimo Over-the-Air Computation
authors: Yaru Wang, Deyou Zhang, Qingchao Li, Jun Liu, Chuang Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) enables low-latency wireless data aggregation, but its accuracy is limited by imperfect signal alignment over fading channels and receiver noise. Fully digital beamforming improves aggregation accuracy in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) AirComp systems but requires one radio-frequency (RF) chain per antenna. To reduce this hardware burden, we investigate microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC)-aided beamforming for MIMO AirComp. Under a lossless and reciprocal MiLAC model, we jointly optimize the transmit digital precoding matrices and the receive-side MiLAC aggregation matrix to minimize the mean squared error (MSE). An alternating optimization algorithm is developed, in which the precoding matrices are optimally updated using the Karush--Kuhn--Tucker conditions and bisection, while the resulting convex aggregation matrix subproblem is solved globally using projected gradient descent. Numerical results verify the algorithm's convergence and demonstrate that MiLAC-aided beamforming approaches the MSE performance of fully digital beamforming with substantially fewer RF chains and outperforms phase-shifter-based hybrid beamforming under the same RF-chain budget.
tldr: This paper proposes a MiLAC-aided beamforming scheme for MIMO over-the-air computation to reduce RF chains while maintaining aggregation accuracy.
motivation: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) suffers from signal misalignment and noise, and fully digital beamforming requires many RF chains, which is hardware-intensive.
method: The authors jointly optimize transmit digital precoding and receive MiLAC aggregation matrix to minimize MSE, using alternating optimization with KKT conditions and projected gradient descent.
result: Numerical results show MiLAC-aided beamforming approaches fully digital performance with fewer RF chains and outperforms phase-shifter-based hybrid beamforming.
conclusion: MiLAC-aided beamforming offers a hardware-efficient solution for MIMO AirComp, balancing performance and complexity.

title: Predissociation Dynamics Of Charged Long-range Rydberg Molecules
authors: Neethu Abraham, P. Giannakeas, Matthew T. Eiles
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate predissociation in homonuclear ([MATH]Rb[MATH][MATH]Rb[MATH]) and heteronuclear ([MATH]Rb[MATH][MATH]Li[MATH]) long-range Rydberg atom-ion molecules. Owing to their micron-scale bond lengths, these dissociate on time scales far removed from those of more tightly bound diatomic molecules. We employ the eigenchannel [MATH]-matrix method to compute predissociation rates for a broad range of principal quantum numbers [MATH]. The rates depend strongly on the mass, but more remarkably display a rapid and periodic variation as a function of [MATH] as well as within a single vibrational ladder. A semiclassical Landau-Zener-St\"uckelberg analysis reveals that St\"uckelberg interference governs the decay process and produces the observed variation in the molecular lifetime. Although the heavy mass of the homonuclear Rb molecule constrains its predissociation rates to a sub-kHz level, the lighter molecule [MATH]Rb[MATH][MATH]Li[MATH] dissociates on time scales competitive with radiative and collisional decay. This can enable in situ study of non-adiabatic decay via ion microscopy.
tldr: This paper studies predissociation dynamics of long-range Rydberg molecules, focusing on quantum interference effects in their decay rates.
motivation: Understanding the decay dynamics of long-range Rydberg molecules is important for their potential applications in quantum technologies, but the paper is primarily a molecular physics study.
method: The authors use the eigenchannel R-matrix method to compute predissociation rates and a semiclassical Landau-Zener-Stückelberg analysis to interpret the results.
result: They find that predissociation rates vary rapidly and periodically with principal quantum number and vibrational level, governed by Stückelberg interference, with lighter molecules dissociating faster.
conclusion: The study provides insights into non-adiabatic decay in Rydberg molecules, but it does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Identifiability-aware Neural Ordinary Differential Equations For Parsimonious And Reliable Dynamic Modelling
authors: Eva Balsa-Canto N\'uria Campo-Manzanares
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural ordinary differential equations (NODE) and hybrid NODE models provide flexible continuous-time representations of complex dynamic systems, but their expressive capacity can exceed the information content of the available data. Consequently, these models may reproduce observed trajectories while retaining weakly identifiable parameters, poorly constrained neural components, and unreliable extrapolation. Here we introduce identifiability-aware neural ordinary differential equations (iNODE), a framework that incorporates practical identifiability into neural differential equation design. iNODE models embed neural components as explicit analytic functions within the governing equations, enabling direct sensitivity analysis, Fisher-information-based confidence intervals, and identifiability-aware architecture selection. Candidate architectures are generated under data-support constraints, jointly calibrated, and ranked according to predictive accuracy, parsimony, and parameter identifiability. We evaluate the complete iNODE workflow against conventional NODE and hybrid NODE workflows representative of current practice using four controlled ground-truth benchmarks spanning fully data-driven and hybrid formulations, latent time-varying parameters, partial observability, and sparse or noisy measurements. Using the same training data and evaluation scenarios, the iNODE workflow selected more compact architectures, reduced parameter uncertainty, and improved extrapolation and recovery from latent-dynamics. These results establish practical identifiability as a model-design principle for parsimonious and reliable neural differential equations.
tldr: This paper introduces identifiability-aware neural ordinary differential equations (iNODE) for parsimonious and reliable dynamic modeling, focusing on parameter identifiability in hybrid neural differential equations.
motivation: Neural ODEs can overfit data and produce unreliable models due to weakly identifiable parameters and poorly constrained neural components.
method: iNODE embeds neural components as explicit analytic functions, enabling sensitivity analysis, Fisher-information-based confidence intervals, and identifiability-aware architecture selection under data-support constraints.
result: On four benchmarks, iNODE selected more compact architectures, reduced parameter uncertainty, and improved extrapolation and recovery from latent dynamics compared to conventional NODE workflows.
conclusion: Practical identifiability is established as a model-design principle for building parsimonious and reliable neural differential equations.

title: Tcad Cryogenic Model Parameters Calibration Based On 65 Nm Nmos Experimental Data
authors: Wesley Xi, Vikram Magendar, Alhaji A Sharka, Hiu Yung Wong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, 65 nm n-type Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect-Transistors (nMOSFETs) are taped out and measured at 292 K to 4.5 K. Technology Computer-Aided-Design (TCAD) model parameters are then calibrated to fit the simulation curves to experimental electrical curves. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is used to unveil the dimensions of the transistors to ensure accurate modeling. The experimental and simulation capacitance-voltage (CV) curves, drain current - gate voltage (IDVG) curves, and drain current - drain voltage (IDVD) curves are fitted well using the calibrated parameters. The major models calibrated are the Lucent model, which is comprised of an extended PhuMob model, Lombardi model for surface mobility, and the H\"ansch high field mobility model. A band-tail model with adjusted band width is applied to fit the sub-threshold swings at all temperatures. The calibrated parameters are expected to be applicable to other technologies because TCAD models are not technology-specific. It is also found that, except for saturation velocity, no new temperature-dependent model is needed. The calibration process and fitting strategies are detailed and are expected to be applicable to calibrate other transistor types.
tldr: This paper calibrates TCAD model parameters for 65 nm nMOSFETs using experimental data from 292 K to 4.5 K, focusing on cryogenic device modeling.
motivation: To enable accurate simulation of cryogenic CMOS devices, which are important for quantum computing control electronics, by calibrating TCAD models to experimental data.
method: The authors fabricated 65 nm nMOSFETs, measured electrical characteristics at various temperatures, used TEM to determine device dimensions, and calibrated TCAD model parameters (Lucent, PhuMob, Lombardi, H"ansch, band-tail) to fit simulation to experiment.
result: The calibrated models accurately reproduce CV, IDVG, and IDVD curves across temperatures from 292 K to 4.5 K, and it was found that no new temperature-dependent models are needed except for saturation velocity.
conclusion: The calibration process is detailed and expected to be applicable to other transistor types and technologies, aiding cryogenic circuit design for quantum systems.

title: Neveu--Schwarz Irregular Vertex Operators, Decomposition Theorems, And Bilinear Operators
authors: Hajime Nagoya
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct rank-zero irregular vertex operators for the Neveu--Schwarz algebra as linear maps between irregular Verma modules of the same rank satisfying the usual superconformal commutation relations and an irregular asymptotic condition. Under the nondegeneracy assumption [MATH], we prove their existence and uniqueness. We then extend the decomposition theorem for the Neveu--Schwarz algebra to the irregular setting: the tensor product of the free-fermion Fock module with a rank-[MATH] Neveu--Schwarz irregular Verma module decomposes into an infinite direct sum of tensor products of two Virasoro irregular Verma modules. We also prove a compatible decomposition of the irregular vertex operators into tensor products of Virasoro irregular vertex operators. Using suitable pairings and mode insertions, we derive bilinear differential equations for weighted sums of products of Virasoro irregular conformal blocks of types [MATH] and [MATH]. After explicit parameter identifications and a gauge transformation in the Painlev\'e V case, the resulting bilinear differential operators agree with those appearing in the quantum Painlev\'e V and IV tau-function equations.
tldr: This paper constructs irregular vertex operators for the Neveu-Schwarz algebra and derives bilinear differential equations related to quantum Painlevé equations.
motivation: The paper aims to extend the theory of irregular vertex operators and decomposition theorems to the Neveu-Schwarz superconformal algebra, with applications to conformal field theory and integrable systems.
method: The authors construct rank-zero irregular vertex operators as linear maps between irregular Verma modules, prove existence and uniqueness under nondegeneracy, and extend decomposition theorems. They then derive bilinear differential equations via pairings and mode insertions.
result: They obtain bilinear differential operators that match those in quantum Painlevé V and IV tau-function equations after parameter identifications and gauge transformations.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous construction of irregular vertex operators in the Neveu-Schwarz setting and connects them to Painlevé equations, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: From Lie--Rinehart Algebras To $F$-Manifold Algebras
authors: Yunhe Sheng Yufeng Pei
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every Lie--Rinehart algebra, we construct an [MATH]-manifold algebra on the direct sum of its base algebra and module. Contrary to the assertion in \cite[Proposition 13.3.26]{LodayVallette}, the resulting structure is generally not Poisson. We determine when powers of the positive-degree ideal in the associated symmetric Poisson algebra are Poisson ideals, and relate the Leibnizator to the Lie--Rinehart differential. For a finite projective module of constant rank, the trace of the Leibnizator recovers the anchor and yields a rigidity result for injective anchors. We conclude with algebraic and geometric examples.
tldr: This paper constructs F-manifold algebras from Lie-Rinehart algebras, correcting a claim about Poisson structures.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the relationship between Lie-Rinehart algebras and F-manifold algebras, addressing an error in a standard reference.
method: They construct an F-manifold algebra on the direct sum of the base algebra and module, analyze Poisson ideal conditions, and relate the Leibnizator to the Lie-Rinehart differential.
result: They show the resulting structure is generally not Poisson, determine when powers of the positive-degree ideal are Poisson ideals, and recover the anchor from the trace of the Leibnizator for finite projective modules.
conclusion: The work provides algebraic and geometric examples, contributing to the theory of F-manifold algebras but not directly to the user's research areas.

title: A Discrete Duality Finite Volume Method With Harmonic Average For Semiconductor Drift-diffusion Equations
authors: Shuya Liu, Zhicheng Liu, Bo Lin, Chijie Zhuang, Qingyuan Shi, Weizhu Bao, Rong Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stationary drift-diffusion model is widely used to model charge transport in semiconductor devices. Classical methods, such as the finite volume Scharfetter--Gummel (FVSG) method, perform well on high-quality Delaunay meshes but struggle on irregular or distorted meshes due to their reliance on Voronoi diagrams. To overcome this mesh limitation, this article introduces a new approach that integrates harmonic average stabilization into the discrete duality finite volume method (DDFV-HA). To validate our scheme, we compare DDFV-HA and FVSG for semiconductor simulations on both high- and low-quality meshes. Experiments show that DDFV-HA matches FVSG on high-quality meshes and is more reliable and accurate on low-quality meshes. Applying DDFV-HA to a real-world thyristor further confirms that it is well-suited for semiconductor simulations in complex, irregular domains where high-quality meshes are not easy to generate.
tldr: This paper introduces a numerical method for semiconductor drift-diffusion equations, which is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The paper aims to improve numerical simulation of semiconductor devices on irregular meshes, which is a classical applied mathematics problem.
method: The authors propose a discrete duality finite volume method with harmonic average stabilization (DDFV-HA) and compare it with the finite volume Scharfetter-Gummel method.
result: DDFV-HA matches FVSG on high-quality meshes and is more reliable and accurate on low-quality meshes, as demonstrated on a thyristor simulation.
conclusion: The method is well-suited for semiconductor simulations in complex domains, but it has no connection to quantum information or related fields.

title: Bioinspired Microactuators Fabricated Via One-step Meniscus-guided 3d Nanoprinting
authors: Seong-Jae Eom, Vasanthan Devaraj, Sunghyun Kwak, Hyeon-Seok Seo, Thomas Zentgraf, Won-Geun Kim, Jong-Min Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a bioinspired microactuator fabricated via a one-step meniscus guided 3D nanoprinting technique. This technique directly produces a freestanding three dimensional composite architecture by integrating a rigid nanoparticle framework with a hygroscopic polymer matrix in a single, assembly free process. Inspired by the functional integration of rigid and compliant components in insect exoskeletal joint, our design synergistically combines load-bearing strength and humidity-driven swelling in a single microscale pillar. Comprehensive experiments, including comparative control structures and microscopic analysis, elucidated the actuation mechanism: the nanoparticle scaffold provides mechanical support while the polymeric phase provides volumetric expansion, yielding large reversible elongation under humidity with preserved structural integrity. The resulting AuNP PVP microactuator shows humidity responsive actuation at the microscale, with representative demonstrations of repeated humidity cycling and load lifting up to approximately 800 times its estimated own weight under the tested conditions. Variant geometries such as hinged pillars demonstrate how axial swelling can be converted into bending motion, and an optical configuration shows how actuation can modulate reflected light signals. This nanoprinting approach provides a simple strategy for constructing bioinspired soft microactuators with humidity-responsive deformation and potential applicability in microscale sensing, optical modulation, and adaptive microdevices.
tldr: This paper presents a bioinspired microactuator fabricated via meniscus-guided 3D nanoprinting, which responds to humidity and can lift heavy loads, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to create a simple, assembly-free method for fabricating bioinspired soft microactuators that combine mechanical strength and humidity-driven actuation, inspired by insect exoskeletal joints.
method: They use a one-step meniscus-guided 3D nanoprinting technique to integrate a rigid nanoparticle framework (AuNP) with a hygroscopic polymer matrix (PVP) into a freestanding composite pillar, and characterize its actuation via experiments and microscopy.
result: The resulting microactuator exhibits large reversible elongation under humidity, can lift loads up to ~800 times its own weight, and can be designed with hinged geometries to convert swelling into bending, as well as modulate reflected light.
conclusion: The nanoprinting approach offers a simple strategy for constructing bioinspired soft microactuators with potential applications in sensing, optical modulation, and adaptive microdevices, but it has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: A Unified Reconstruction Algorithm For Reduced-frame Structured Illumination Microscopy
authors: Jingxiang Zhang, Tianyu Zhao, Manming Shu, Keru Mou, Zheming Zhang, Yihan Sun, Mengrui Wang, Yansheng Liang, Shaowei Wang, Ming Lei
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reduced-frame structured illumination microscopy (SIM) is attractive for live-cell imaging because it can improve temporal throughput and reduce photobleaching, but incomplete phase sampling makes reconstruction unstable and computationally demanding. Here we present URA-SIM, a unified reduced-acquisition framework that turns fixed reduced-frame measurements into pipeline- compatible raw stacks through model-consistent phase-domain completion. Instead of solving a large object-level inverse problem or replacing established SIM reconstruction, URA-SIM estimates the missing phase content on the low-dimensional phase-harmonic manifold required by the target modality and then delegates order separation and image formation to classical reconstruction pipeline. This design combines three practical advantages: fidelity from the SIM forward structure, lightweight online computation, and direct compatibility with existing reconstruction workflows. For 2D-SIM, URA-SIM uses the first-harmonic phase structure of three-phase SIM to estimate a shared zero-order field and complete missing phase samples by direction-wise harmonic fitting. On calibration and biological 2D-SIM data, reduced-frame reconstructions preserve resolvable structures and remain competitive on COS7 mitochondria comparison data. In live-cell COS7 mitochondria imaging, URA-SIM reconstructs each time point from five acquired raw frames and resolves mitochondrial cristae across different temporal sampling regimes. Experiments on 3D-SIM and nonlinear SIM further show that the same design principle can be transferred when the phase model and reconstruction-pipeline interface are adapted to the target modality. These results support URA-SIM as a transparent, model-consistent and computationally lightweight route from fixed reduced-frame acquisition to classical SIM reconstruction workflows.
tldr: This paper presents a unified reconstruction algorithm for reduced-frame structured illumination microscopy, a computational imaging technique unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to improve temporal resolution and reduce photobleaching in live-cell imaging by developing a reconstruction method for reduced-frame SIM data.
method: URA-SIM estimates missing phase content on a low-dimensional phase-harmonic manifold and integrates with classical SIM reconstruction pipelines.
result: The method preserves resolvable structures in 2D-SIM, 3D-SIM, and nonlinear SIM, and resolves mitochondrial cristae in live-cell imaging.
conclusion: URA-SIM offers a computationally lightweight and model-consistent approach for reduced-frame SIM, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: New Optimal Linear Codes Over $\zz_4$
authors: Djoko Suprijanto Hopein Christofen Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present novel approaches for constructing linear codes over [MATH] from the known ones. We succeeded in obtaining new linear codes, many of which are optimal. In particular, we found all optimal codes for [MATH] and many optimal codes for [MATH].
tldr: This paper presents new constructions of optimal linear codes over the ring Z4, which is a topic in classical coding theory without direct quantum information or thermodynamics relevance.
motivation: The authors aim to construct new linear codes over Z4, many of which are optimal, to advance classical coding theory.
method: They propose novel approaches for constructing linear codes over Z4 from known ones, likely using algebraic or combinatorial techniques.
result: They obtained new linear codes, including all optimal codes for certain parameters and many optimal codes for others.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical coding theory but does not connect to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: A Kronecker-Weyl Theorem From Interpolation Sets
authors: Rafael Reno S. Cantuba
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An analog of the classical Kronecker-Weyl theorem for weak uniform distribution is obtained for an arbitrary countably infinite independent subset of a discrete abelian group using a type of interpolation sets called epsilon-Kronecker sets. Specifically, the topological size of the set of homomorphisms inducing weakly uniformly distributed sequences is established by showing that it forms a dense G-delta set.
tldr: This paper proves a Kronecker-Weyl theorem analog for weakly uniformly distributed sequences using epsilon-Kronecker sets in discrete abelian groups.
motivation: The paper aims to extend classical results on uniform distribution to a more general setting, using interpolation sets to characterize homomorphisms that induce weakly uniformly distributed sequences.
method: The author employs epsilon-Kronecker sets, a type of interpolation set, to establish that the set of homomorphisms inducing weakly uniformly distributed sequences is a dense G-delta set.
result: The main result shows that for any countably infinite independent subset of a discrete abelian group, the set of homomorphisms yielding weak uniform distribution is topologically large (dense G-delta).
conclusion: This provides a new analog of the Kronecker-Weyl theorem, contributing to the theory of uniform distribution in topological groups.

title: Channel Estimation For Otfs Systems With Overspread Doppler Shifts
authors: Preety Priya, Yi Hong, Emanuele Viterbo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider an orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) system in time-varying channels with overspread Doppler shifts, typically found in non-terrestrial multi-satellite links. The overspread Doppler shifts with magnitude greater than half of the subcarrier spacing, result in aliased Doppler shifts in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain due to the OTFS modulo operation. This makes channel estimation very challenging and the traditional channel estimation methods become ineffective. To address this challenge, we propose a DD training frame and a two-stage channel estimation method. The training frame comprises a cosine pilot signal and a pilot symbol. In the first stage of the channel estimation, the pilot symbol in the DD domain is utilized to estimate the delays, aliased Doppler shifts, and channel gains of the propagation paths. In the second stage, the received time domain signal is converted into the frequency domain to detect the peaks of all the Doppler shifts using the cosine pilot signal. Then, we present a threshold-based method to pair the estimated actual Doppler shifts with their corresponding delays and channel gains. The complexity of the proposed channel estimation is also discussed. Finally, the performance of the proposed channel estimation is validated in terms of the normalized mean square error (NMSE) and bit error rate (BER) in various scenarios.
tldr: This paper proposes a channel estimation method for OTFS systems with overspread Doppler shifts, focusing on wireless communication signal processing.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of channel estimation in OTFS systems when Doppler shifts exceed half the subcarrier spacing, causing aliasing in the delay-Doppler domain, which is common in non-terrestrial multi-satellite links.
method: The method uses a DD training frame with a cosine pilot and a pilot symbol, employing a two-stage estimation: first estimating delays, aliased Doppler shifts, and gains from the pilot symbol, then detecting actual Doppler peaks from the cosine pilot in the frequency domain, followed by a threshold-based pairing.
result: The proposed method is validated via NMSE and BER simulations in various scenarios, showing improved performance over traditional methods.
conclusion: The paper concludes that the proposed two-stage channel estimation effectively handles overspread Doppler shifts, providing reliable channel estimation for OTFS systems in such challenging environments.

title: On Nearly-Perfect Covering Codes Beyond Radius One
authors: Moshe Schwartz Gabriel Sac Himelfarb
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study (binary) nearly-perfect covering codes, which are codes that attain the Van Wee bound with equality. They act as the covering counterparts to nearly-perfect error-correcting codes, which attain the Johnson bound with equality. These codes have been completely classified for covering radius [MATH]. We prove that no code with [MATH] can attain the original Van Wee bound with equality, since it omits the dependence on the minimum distance of the code. We refine the bound to account for the minimum distance and show some nearly-perfect covering codes. By proving some structural properties of such codes, we prove all nearly-perfect covering codes with [MATH] must be equivalent to the codes we showed. We also prove that for any [MATH], there are at most a finite number of nearly-perfect covering codes.
tldr: This paper studies nearly-perfect covering codes, a topic in classical coding theory, and proves structural results about them.
motivation: The authors aim to classify nearly-perfect covering codes beyond radius one, which are codes that attain the Van Wee bound with equality.
method: They refine the Van Wee bound to account for minimum distance and prove structural properties of such codes.
result: They show that no code with certain parameters can attain the original Van Wee bound, and they classify all nearly-perfect covering codes with a given radius.
conclusion: The paper contributes to classical coding theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Local Finiteness Of The Number Of Reflections In Semi-dispersing Minkowski Billiards
authors: Sergei Ivanov Roman Barinov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that in a semi-dispersing Minkowski billiard, that is a billiard in the complement of a collection of convex sets in a normed space with a smooth strictly convex norm, any billiard trajectory of finite length has only finitely many reflections off the walls.
tldr: This paper proves a finiteness result for reflections in semi-dispersing Minkowski billiards, a topic in dynamical systems and geometry.
motivation: The authors aim to establish a fundamental property of billiard trajectories in normed spaces with convex obstacles, which is relevant to the study of dynamical systems and geometric optics.
method: The proof likely uses geometric arguments and properties of convex sets and norms to show that any finite-length trajectory can only have finitely many reflections.
result: The main result is that in semi-dispersing Minkowski billiards, every finite-length trajectory has only finitely many reflections off the walls.
conclusion: This contributes to the mathematical theory of billiards, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Universality Of E-detectors For Arl Control
authors: Aaditya Ramdas

Thresholding e-detectors controls the average run length (ARL): declaring a change at the first time [MATH] when [MATH] crosses [MATH] ensures that [MATH]. But e-detectors do substantially more than control the ARL; they also satisfy a : \[ P(T_b\leq\sigma)\leq \mathbb E_P[\sigma]/b \] for every data-dependent stopping time (monitoring horizon) \(\sigma\) and [MATH]. In particular, every e-detector-based procedure obeys [MATH] at each fixed [MATH], thus avoiding early false alarms. Remarkably, the converse also holds: every stopping time [MATH] that satisfies the optional-horizon inequality must in fact arise from thresholding an e-detector.
