title: An Algebraic Method For Optimizing The State, Control, And Terminal State Weight Matrices For Optimal Feedback Control
authors: Daegyun Choi, Donghoon Kim, James D. Turner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The necessary conditions for formulating optimal feedback control algorithms have been known for many years. Free parameters exist in the performance index in the form of state and control penalty and terminal state penalty matrices for tuning the performance of the optimally controlled system. The selection process is typically experimental and iterative. To generate the weight matrices for optimal feedback control algorithms, an optimization process is proposed. Typically, the optimization process for the weight matrices requires several numerical integration processes that are computationally expensive; this work overcomes the classical high computational cost by exploiting closed-form solutions for the time-varying Riccati matrix, state trajectories, state transition matrix, and the optimal performance index. Closed-form algebraic equations are used to generate all partial derivative calculations, and no numerical integration is required. The closed-form partial derivatives are used to generate analytic gradients for the optimization steps. The optimization strategy seeks to minimize the terminal state values for the feedback control problem. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimization algorithm. The resulting computational procedures are expected to be broadly useful for control theory applications in science and engineering.
tldr: This paper proposes an algebraic optimization method for selecting weight matrices in optimal feedback control, using closed-form solutions to avoid numerical integration.
motivation: The selection of state, control, and terminal state weight matrices in optimal feedback control is typically iterative and computationally expensive. The authors aim to provide a more efficient optimization approach.
method: The method exploits closed-form solutions for the time-varying Riccati matrix, state trajectories, state transition matrix, and optimal performance index to compute analytic gradients, eliminating the need for numerical integration.
result: A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed optimization algorithm in minimizing terminal state values.
conclusion: The proposed algebraic method offers a computationally efficient way to optimize weight matrices for optimal feedback control, with potential broad applicability in control theory.

title: Efficient Hessian-Free Methods For Multi-Objective Bilevel Optimization With Nonconvex Lower Level
authors: Feihu Huang Yicong Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-objective bilevel optimization has wide applications in the AI area such as automated learning and multi-task meta-learning. Although recently some works have been begun to study the multi-objective bilevel optimization, the proposed methods rely on the (strongly) convex lower level problems. In fact, these multi-objective bilevel learning problems are generally nonconvex, and particularly their lower level problems are nonconvex. To fill this gap, we propose a class of Multi-Objective Moreau Envelope based Hessian-free Algorithms (MOMEHA) to solve the multi-objective bilevel learning problems with nonconvex lower level. Specifically, our method uses the Moreau envelope to convert the original problem into a multi-objective single-level optimization with an envelope constraint. In particular, our method retains computational advantages of being single-loop and Hessian-free in the multi-objective setting by incorporating a smooth weighted Tchebycheff scalarization. Furthermore, we propose a momentum-based variant of MOMEHA (i.e., MB-MOMEHA) method to solve the stochastic multi-objective bilevel learning problems. In theory, we provide the convergence properties of our algorithms under both deterministic and stochastic setting. Some experiments on few-shot meta-learning and neural architecture search demonstrate that our methods outperform the existing approaches in Pareto front, validating its effectiveness and robustness.
tldr: This paper proposes efficient Hessian-free algorithms for multi-objective bilevel optimization with nonconvex lower-level problems, applied to meta-learning and neural architecture search.
motivation: Existing multi-objective bilevel optimization methods assume convex lower-level problems, but many real-world AI applications have nonconvex lower levels. The authors aim to fill this gap.
method: They introduce Multi-Objective Moreau Envelope based Hessian-free Algorithms (MOMEHA) that convert the bilevel problem into a single-level optimization with an envelope constraint, using smooth weighted Tchebycheff scalarization to maintain single-loop and Hessian-free properties. A momentum-based variant (MB-MOMEHA) is also proposed for stochastic settings.
result: Theoretical convergence guarantees are provided for both deterministic and stochastic settings. Experiments on few-shot meta-learning and neural architecture search show improved Pareto front compared to existing methods.
conclusion: The proposed methods effectively solve nonconvex multi-objective bilevel optimization problems, demonstrating practical utility in AI applications.

title: The Mixed Spectral Problem For Radial Schr\"{o}dinger Operators And Paley-Wiener Spaces
authors: Yongjiang Duan, Yufei Li, Zeguang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inverse spectral problem for the radial Schr\"{o}dinger operators on the finite interval is investigated. The potential is recovered from the given eigenvalues plus its information on a smaller interval. The method is to discuss the connections between the Paley-Wiener spaces and the potentials, from which we completely determine the potential on the whole interval from the potential on a smaller interval and a set of eigenvalues in terms of the complete exponential systems.
tldr: This paper investigates the inverse spectral problem for radial Schrödinger operators, connecting Paley-Wiener spaces to recover potentials from partial data.
motivation: The authors aim to solve an inverse spectral problem for radial Schrödinger operators, where the potential is recovered from eigenvalues and information on a smaller interval.
method: They use connections between Paley-Wiener spaces and potentials, employing complete exponential systems to determine the potential on the whole interval.
result: They completely determine the potential on the whole interval from the potential on a smaller interval and a set of eigenvalues.
conclusion: The paper provides a mathematical solution to a specific inverse problem, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Hyper-V Uniform Ergodicity Of Markov Chains
authors: Kshitij Khare Austin Brown
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a new uniform drift condition and local minorization that implies a stronger weighted form of uniform ergodicity for Markov chains we call hyper-V uniform ergodicity. The convergence guarantees geometric decay of the bias towards the invariant measure independently of the initialization for all functions controlled by a dominating function V. A key advantage of the approach is that it bypasses the need to establish a global minorization condition, which is often substantially more difficult to verify in practice, while yielding stronger convergence guarantees than global minorization. Optimal convergence bounds in a minimax sense of the framework are established. The utility of the framework is demonstrated through applications to the P'olya-Gamma and Kolmogorov-Gamma Gibbs samplers. We also show qualitative hyper-V uniform ergodicity convergence for two-variable Gibbs samplers can be inferred by the form of the invariant measure, bypassing convergence analysis entirely.
tldr: This paper introduces a new uniform drift condition for Markov chains that yields hyper-V uniform ergodicity, with applications to Gibbs samplers.
motivation: The authors aim to provide stronger convergence guarantees for Markov chains without requiring a global minorization condition, which is often difficult to verify.
method: They develop a uniform drift condition and local minorization that imply hyper-V uniform ergodicity, and establish optimal convergence bounds in a minimax sense.
result: The framework is applied to Pólya-Gamma and Kolmogorov-Gamma Gibbs samplers, and qualitative convergence for two-variable Gibbs samplers is inferred from the invariant measure.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical alternative to global minorization for proving uniform ergodicity, with stronger guarantees and broad applicability to Gibbs samplers.

title: Shape Design For Degenerate Hyperbolic Equation With Degenerate Boundary And Its Application To Observability
authors: Yuanzhi Zhou Dong-Hui Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the observability and controllability of a class of degenerate hyperbolic equations with a control region intersecting the degenerate set. Unlike the existing results that mainly deal with control regions separated from the degeneracy, we consider the case where the control region reaches the degenerate part. To handle the difficulty caused by the degeneracy, we introduce a shape-design-based approximation method based on shape design by approximating the degenerate equation with a family of uniformly hyperbolic equations. The proof relies on the spectral approximation of the associated operators, precise estimates for weak solutions, and the multiplier method. We first establish observability inequalities for the approximating equations with constants independent of the approximation parameter. Then, by passing to the degenerate limit, we obtain the observability inequality for the original degenerate equation.
tldr: This paper studies observability and controllability of degenerate hyperbolic equations with control regions intersecting the degeneracy, using a shape-design-based approximation method.
motivation: The paper addresses a gap in control theory for degenerate hyperbolic equations where the control region reaches the degenerate set, which is more challenging than the separated case.
method: The authors introduce a shape-design-based approximation method, approximating the degenerate equation with uniformly hyperbolic equations, and use spectral approximation, weak solution estimates, and the multiplier method.
result: They establish observability inequalities for the approximating equations with constants independent of the approximation parameter, and then pass to the limit to obtain the observability inequality for the original degenerate equation.
conclusion: The work provides a new approach to handle degeneracy in hyperbolic control problems, extending observability results to cases where control regions intersect the degenerate set.

title: Difference-of-Convex Regularization For Graph Learning By Differentiable Programming
authors: Chee Wei Tan Liping Tao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laplacian-regularized minimization is fundamental in signal processing and machine learning, but is limited by the dense and ill-conditioned nature of the graph Laplacian pseudoinverse. While the Laplacian itself is sparse, its pseudoinverse is dense and often ill-conditioned, rendering direct computation impractical at scale. Moreover, pseudoinverse learning is more challenging than Laplacian learning. To address this challenge, this paper considers the setting where the graph Laplacian is given and proposes a Difference-of-Convex Regularizer (DCR) graph learning framework that approximates the spectral action of the Laplacian pseudoinverse without direct inversion via regularized Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE). By reformulating Laplacian-Regularized Nonnegative Least Squares (LR-NNLS) through a dual representation, DCR decouples pseudoinverse learning from instance-specific inference and enables efficient primal solution reconstruction via a differentiable dual-guided learning scheme. We establish theoretical guarantees on stability and the existence of a unique fixed point for DCR algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved performance over convex solvers and graph filtering baselines and robust performance across diverse graph topologies.
tldr: This paper proposes a difference-of-convex regularization framework for graph learning that approximates the Laplacian pseudoinverse without direct inversion.
motivation: The graph Laplacian pseudoinverse is dense and ill-conditioned, making direct computation impractical at scale, and pseudoinverse learning is more challenging than Laplacian learning.
method: The authors reformulate Laplacian-regularized nonnegative least squares via a dual representation, decoupling pseudoinverse learning from instance-specific inference, and use a differentiable dual-guided learning scheme for efficient primal solution reconstruction.
result: Theoretical guarantees on stability and existence of a unique fixed point are established, and numerical experiments show improved performance over convex solvers and graph filtering baselines across diverse graph topologies.
conclusion: The DCR framework offers an efficient and robust approach to graph learning with Laplacian regularization, avoiding direct pseudoinverse computation.

title: Mean Field Stackelberg Game For Production And Carbon Emission Reduction With State Reflections
authors: Lijun Bo, Zhen Liu, Jingfei Wang, Jiacheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global warming, driven by anthropogenic carbon emissions with transboundary pollution characteristics and irreversible damage, poses an existential threat to human society. This paper develops a novel two-level Stackelberg game with mean field interaction of controls and common noise which integrates hierarchical decision-making under a state-reflected emission dynamics. A central regulator (leader) adjusts product prices to guide [MATH] heterogeneous competing regions (followers) while enforcing a hard emission cap via a reflection mechanism that models emergency reductions through a local time process. We establish the existence of an approximate Stackelberg equilibrium and perform sensitivity analysis via Monte Carlo simulations.
tldr: This paper develops a mean field Stackelberg game for production and carbon emission reduction with state reflections, focusing on economic and environmental policy rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses global warming and carbon emissions, aiming to model hierarchical decision-making between a regulator and heterogeneous regions under emission caps.
method: It formulates a two-level Stackelberg game with mean field interaction and common noise, incorporating a state-reflected emission dynamics with a local time process for emergency reductions.
result: The authors establish the existence of an approximate Stackelberg equilibrium and perform sensitivity analysis via Monte Carlo simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for policy design in carbon emission reduction, but it is unrelated to the specified research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Feature-Based Continuation Of Pattern Transitions In A One-Dimensional Brusselator
authors: Qiushi Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Different long-time patterns can prevail in different regions of a reaction--diffusion system's parameter space. We study the transition curves between such regimes for a one-dimensional Brusselator in the two-parameter plane [MATH], focusing on wave/stripe-like, spiral/source-defect-like, and target-like states. We develop a feature-based continuation framework built on time-dependent PDE simulations. Scalar observables extracted from late-time solution data distinguish the regimes and define threshold level sets where the feature crossings are regular. A secant predictor and a local one-dimensional sweep corrector are used to trace these level sets. For the spiral transition, we introduce a branch-adapted spacetime symmetry-defect feature that separates asymmetric source-like patterns from more symmetric wave patterns. For the target transition, we use the minimum of a core spatial-variance score and a tail temporal-variance score to detect the characteristic structure of half-target states. The method recovers robust side portions of both transition curves. In lower parameter regions, where mixed and irregular patterns make a single scalar feature less specific, we instead report transition estimates obtained from vertical parameter sweeps and direct inspection of spacetime plots. These results show how simulation-based continuation and direct pattern classification can be combined to map regime boundaries while preserving the different levels of numerical evidence.
tldr: This paper develops a feature-based continuation method to trace pattern transition curves in a one-dimensional Brusselator reaction-diffusion system.
motivation: The study aims to map regime boundaries between different long-time patterns in a reaction-diffusion system, which is a topic in nonlinear dynamics and pattern formation.
method: The method combines time-dependent PDE simulations with scalar observables extracted from late-time data, using a secant predictor and local sweeps to trace transition curves.
result: The method successfully recovers side portions of transition curves for spiral and target patterns, while lower parameter regions require direct sweeps and inspection.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a simulation-based continuation approach for mapping pattern transitions, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Feedback Diagonalization And Stabilization For Discrete Linear Ensemble Systems
authors: Xudong Chen Jonathan M. Bosnich
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a countably infinite collection of linear, scalar control systems, where each system is represented by the pair [MATH] with [MATH] for [MATH], and all systems are forced by a common scalar control input. We refer to this collection of systems as a discrete linear ensemble system. The ensemble system is feedback stabilizable if there exists a common feedback control input that asymptotically stabilizes every system simultaneously. Unlike finite-dimensional linear systems, an infinite-dimensional linear system is not guaranteed to be stable if its poles lie in the open left half-plane. Stability is guaranteed, however, if (i) its poles are contained in the closed left half-plane and (ii) its infinitesimal generator is diagonalizable. In this paper, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a static, linear feedback control law that ensures the closed-loop ensemble system satisfies (i) and (ii). In particular, we show that the exponential decay of the sequences [MATH] and [MATH] is necessary and, under an assumption on the desired poles, sufficient.
tldr: This paper studies feedback stabilization of infinite collections of linear control systems, a topic in control theory with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to provide necessary and sufficient conditions for feedback stabilizability of discrete linear ensemble systems, addressing a gap in infinite-dimensional control theory.
method: They analyze the closed-loop system's stability by examining the poles of the infinitesimal generator and its diagonalizability, deriving conditions on the exponential decay of system parameters.
result: They show that exponential decay of certain sequences is necessary and, under an assumption on desired poles, sufficient for the existence of a static linear feedback law ensuring stability.
conclusion: The work contributes to control theory but is outside the scope of the user's research interests in quantum information and related areas.

title: Finite Element Approximation Of The Linearized Cahn-Hilliard-Cook Equation
authors: Stig Larsson Ali Mesforush
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The linearized Cahn-Hilliard-Cook equation is discretized in the spatial variables by a standard finite element method. Strong convergence estimates are proved under suitable assumptions on the covariance operator of the Wiener process, which is driving the equation. The backward Euler time stepping is also studied. The analysis is set in a framework based on analytic semigroups. The main effort is spent on proving detailed error bounds for the corresponding deterministic Cahn-Hilliard equation. The results should be interpreted as results on approximation of the stochastic convolution, which is a part of the mild solution of the nonlinear Cahn-Hilliard-Cook equation.
tldr: This paper analyzes finite element discretization of the linearized Cahn-Hilliard-Cook equation, a stochastic partial differential equation, with error estimates for the stochastic convolution.
motivation: The paper aims to provide numerical analysis for a stochastic PDE model, which is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
method: The authors use standard finite element methods for spatial discretization and backward Euler time stepping, with analysis based on analytic semigroups and detailed error bounds for the deterministic Cahn-Hilliard equation.
result: Strong convergence estimates are proved under suitable assumptions on the covariance operator of the Wiener process.
conclusion: The results contribute to numerical analysis of stochastic PDEs but have no connection to quantum information or related fields.

title: Weighted Nuclear Elastic Net Estimation Of (Near-) Low-Rank Drift Matrices In Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Processes
authors: Dmytro Marushkevych, Francisco Pina, Mark Podolskij
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study estimation of the drift matrix in a continuously observed high-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process when the drift is exactly or approximately low rank. In this setting, exact low rank induces non-stable directions and hence a non-ergodic regime, resulting in a poorly conditioned empirical covariance matrix. To address this difficulty, we introduce a Weighted Nuclear Elastic Net Estimator that combines ridge regularization with a nuclear-norm penalty expressed in the empirical likelihood geometry. Under a general diagonalizable spectral framework, we establish oracle inequalities relative to arbitrary low-rank comparison matrices. For near low-rank drifts, the approximation error is naturally measured through the singular-value decay of the drift after weighting by the regularized empirical covariance. The stochastic term is controlled by self-normalized martingale arguments under appropriate choice of the tuning parameter. For a symmetric positive-semidefinite exact low-rank model, we verify the empirical-curvature condition required to translate the weighted bound into a Frobenius-norm bound. With an appropriate choice of tuning parameters, the resulting estimator satisfies, up to a logarithmic factor, the standard rank-[MATH] matrix-estimation scaling [MATH]: specifically, its squared Frobenius error is of order [MATH] with high probability, under an explicit dimension-horizon condition.
tldr: This paper proposes a weighted nuclear elastic net estimator for drift matrices in high-dimensional Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, focusing on statistical estimation theory.
motivation: The authors aim to address the challenge of estimating low-rank drift matrices in non-ergodic high-dimensional OU processes, where the empirical covariance is poorly conditioned.
method: They introduce a Weighted Nuclear Elastic Net Estimator combining ridge and nuclear-norm penalties in the empirical likelihood geometry, and establish oracle inequalities under a diagonalizable spectral framework.
result: The estimator achieves, up to logarithmic factors, the standard rank-matrix estimation scaling for squared Frobenius error under explicit dimension-horizon conditions.
conclusion: The paper contributes to high-dimensional statistical estimation but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Counterexample To Robust Second-Order Convergence Of The Strang Projector-Splitting Integrator
authors: Shiheng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Strang projector-splitting integrator is widely observed to converge with order two, whereas the error analysis that remains uniform as the smallest singular value retained in the low-rank approximation tends to zero proves only order one. We show that this gap is intrinsic under the standard assumptions. We construct [MATH] matrix differential equations that are [MATH] in time and smooth in the matrix variable, with rank-two initial data that satisfy uniform boundedness, Lipschitz, tangency-defect, and regularity bounds. Nevertheless, the exact-subflow Strang method has a nonzero [MATH] term in the local error over one periodic forcing cycle consisting of four Strang steps. Repetition of that cycle rules out a global second-order bound whose constant and stepsize threshold are independent of the retained singular values. The mechanism is a rapid rotation of the factor directions associated with the small singular value: first-order consistency is preserved, but the changing projection spaces prevent the cancellation normally expected from a symmetric Strang composition. Hence the robust first-order result cannot, under these assumptions alone, be upgraded to robust second order for the classical projector-splitting method.
tldr: This paper presents a counterexample showing that the Strang projector-splitting integrator cannot achieve robust second-order convergence under standard assumptions, only first-order.
motivation: The gap between observed second-order convergence and proven first-order uniform error bounds for the Strang projector-splitting integrator is investigated.
method: The author constructs a specific matrix differential equation with rank-two initial data satisfying standard regularity conditions, and analyzes the local error of the exact-subflow Strang method over a periodic forcing cycle.
result: A nonzero second-order term in the local error is found, ruling out a global second-order bound independent of the smallest singular value.
conclusion: The classical projector-splitting method cannot be upgraded to robust second-order convergence under the given assumptions, confirming the intrinsic nature of the gap.

title: Analysis Of Error Propagation In Autoencoder-Based Reduced-Order Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
authors: Gwanghyun Jo Jingyi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural ODE reduced-order models often achieve comparable local prediction accuracy, yet their long-horizon extrapolation behavior can differ substantially. To analyze this discrepancy, we develop a path-integral identity that separates local discrepancy injection from amplification in the learned latent dynamics. The associated multi-step Jacobian norms quantify transport sensitivity and distinguish different propagation regimes. Experiments on the Burgers and Gray--Scott systems exhibit two distinct patterns of error evolution. In Burgers systems, prediction errors remain bounded and are primarily associated with persistent local discrepancies. In contrast, Gray--Scott systems exhibit pronounced amplification during extrapolation, where Jacobian norms serve as sensitivity diagnostics rather than direct indicators of physical prediction accuracy.
tldr: This paper analyzes error propagation in autoencoder-based reduced-order neural ODEs using a path-integral identity and Jacobian norms.
motivation: To understand why neural ODE reduced-order models with similar local accuracy can have different long-horizon extrapolation behavior.
method: Develops a path-integral identity separating local discrepancy injection from amplification, and uses multi-step Jacobian norms to quantify transport sensitivity.
result: Experiments on Burgers and Gray-Scott systems show two error patterns: bounded errors with persistent local discrepancies for Burgers, and pronounced amplification for Gray-Scott where Jacobian norms serve as sensitivity diagnostics.
conclusion: The analysis provides a framework for diagnosing error propagation in reduced-order neural ODEs, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dcba: Detection Of Collaborative Black-Hole Attacks In Connected Dominated Set Using Baiting Process
authors: Venugopal K R Lata B T
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile Ad-hoc Network (MANET) is temporary and dynamic network topology, wherein nodes are mobile in nature and distributed randomly in a network area. In MANET, nodes cooperate with each other to operate and forward data through multihop communication between source and destination. MANET is exposed to different types of attacks due to absence of central administration. However, some nodes decline to cooperate, misbehaves and appears to be malicious affecting network functionality and connectivity. Providing security and identifying malicious node has become one of the challenging research topics in MANET. Black-hole attack is considered to be most popular attack that degrades the overall network performance. Black-hole node falsely advertises the shortest path to destination intentionally to disrupt the network communication resulting in packet drop. In collaborative black-hole attacks, multiple black-hole nodes cooperate and launch attacks in order to degrade network reliability. In this article we propose a Lightweight technique to detect and isolate Collaborative Black-Hole attacks (LW-CBH) by enhancing existing AODV routing protocol. In this scheme a timer based baiting process and reverse tracing setup is used to detect malicious node through control status message in MAC layer which are Reply Sequence (R-SEQ) and Code Sequence (C-SEQ) message of connected dominated set of nodes. However existing AODV routing protocol fails to detect malicious node during dynamic topology changing in MANET. Simulation of proposed technique is performed using discrete event simulator tool NS-2.35. The simulation results are evaluated for throughput, packet delivery ratio, average end-to-end delay and normalized routing overhead.
tldr: This paper proposes a lightweight technique to detect collaborative black-hole attacks in MANETs using a baiting process and connected dominating set, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: MANETs are vulnerable to collaborative black-hole attacks that degrade network performance, and existing AODV routing protocol fails to detect malicious nodes in dynamic topologies.
method: The proposed LW-CBH scheme enhances AODV with a timer-based baiting process and reverse tracing, using control status messages (R-SEQ and C-SEQ) in the MAC layer of connected dominating set nodes to detect and isolate malicious nodes.
result: Simulations in NS-2.35 show improvements in throughput, packet delivery ratio, average end-to-end delay, and normalized routing overhead compared to existing methods.
conclusion: The technique effectively detects and isolates collaborative black-hole attacks in MANETs, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: On The Exponential Circuit Imbalance Of The Ben-Tal Nemirovski Approximation
authors: Stephen Vavasis Jonah Bondar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dadush et al.\ (2024) recently developed a scaling-invariant layered least squares algorithm for linear programming whose complexity depends on the optimal condition measure [MATH]. Their work builds on Vavasis and Ye's (1996) algorithm whose running time depends only on the constraint matrix [MATH] through the condition number [MATH]. The optimal condition measure [MATH] is defined as the minimum [MATH] achievable over all positive diagonal column rescalings [MATH]. Dadush et al.\ (2024) also introduced the optimal circuit imbalance measure [MATH], which serves as a lower bound for [MATH]. Instances with artificially large optimal circuit imbalance measures [MATH] can be easily constructed; however, finding naturally occurring examples where this optimal scaling-invariant measure grows exponentially is of independent interest. In this paper, we show that the Ben-Tal Nemirovski (BN) linear programming approximation of the unit disk provides such an example. By explicitly constructing circuits in the kernel of the BN formulation, we prove that the optimal circuit imbalance measure [MATH] grows exponentially in the number of approximation steps. Since [MATH] lower bounds [MATH], our result demonstrates that the BN approximation yields an exponentially ill-conditioned family of constraint matrices.
tldr: This paper analyzes the exponential growth of the optimal circuit imbalance measure in the Ben-Tal Nemirovski linear programming approximation of the unit disk, showing it yields an exponentially ill-conditioned family of constraint matrices.
motivation: The authors aim to find naturally occurring instances where the optimal circuit imbalance measure grows exponentially, which is of independent interest in the context of linear programming algorithms.
method: They explicitly construct circuits in the kernel of the Ben-Tal Nemirovski formulation and prove that the optimal circuit imbalance measure grows exponentially with the number of approximation steps.
result: The optimal circuit imbalance measure grows exponentially, and since it lower bounds the optimal condition measure, the BN approximation yields an exponentially ill-conditioned family of constraint matrices.
conclusion: The paper provides a concrete example of exponential ill-conditioning in a natural linear programming formulation, which may have implications for the complexity of interior-point methods.

title: Error-Aware Reverse Auction Mechanism For Large Language Model Routing
authors: Haolong Chen, Zhengyuan Xin, Liang Zhang, Lei Xue, Guangxu Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Routing each query to a cost-effective large language model (LLM) is critical for balancing quality and cost, yet most routers rely on a centralized task center to predict model performance, creating an information-risk mismatch and a scalability bottleneck as the model pool grows. We propose a market-based routing paradigm that shifts ex-ante prediction to LLM providers via a reverse auction, where providers bid with self-predicted success probabilities and execution costs. To account for inherently noisy provider predictions and center evaluations, we introduce the rror-ware everse uction echanism} (EA-RAM), which explicitly models this inherent Dual Error. We prove that EA-RAM is Bayesian incentive compatible and individually rational under the Dual Error, establish sufficient conditions for center rationality, and derive an explicit welfare-loss bound. We further identify robustness effects: opposite-signed errors can cancel, vanishing-tail link functions (e.g., logistic) stabilize clear-cut cases via saturation, and extra noise smooths belief maps, reducing the gains from marginal manipulation. Experiments on simulations and real-world benchmarks show that EA-RAM is robust to the Dual Error and achieves a better cost--performance Pareto frontier than centralized baselines, with additional gains when providers contribute local information, validating its practical effectiveness.
tldr: This paper proposes a market-based reverse auction mechanism for routing queries to large language models, focusing on cost-performance trade-offs and incentive compatibility.
motivation: Centralized LLM routers face scalability and information-risk mismatch; the authors aim to shift prediction to providers via a reverse auction.
method: They introduce EA-RAM, a reverse auction mechanism that models dual error in provider predictions and center evaluations, and prove Bayesian incentive compatibility and individual rationality.
result: EA-RAM achieves a better cost-performance Pareto frontier than centralized baselines and is robust to prediction errors.
conclusion: Market-based routing with error-aware mechanisms can improve LLM routing efficiency and robustness.

title: Computing Fixed Points Using Dependency Oracles
authors: Giorgio Bacci, Giovanni Bacci, Kim G. Larsen, Daniele Toller
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present global and local algorithms for solving systems of equations over Noetherian posets with a bottom element, a general setting underlying many verification problems. Our algorithms compute the solution of a selected variable by restricting exploration to those parts of the system required to determine its value. We achieve this by computing variable dependencies by means of dependency oracles. Oracles guide the exploration of the system and provide sound termination criteria for local fixed-point computation. A key advantage of our approach is its flexibility: oracles can be customized, composed, or over-approximated, offering a principled way to trade precision for performance without compromising correctness. We evaluate our solution against existing algorithms from the literature and show that our prototype implementation is competitive and often outperforms specialized solutions, while remaining simple and adaptable across diverse application domains.
tldr: This paper presents algorithms for computing fixed points over Noetherian posets using dependency oracles, with applications to verification problems.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the efficiency of solving systems of equations in verification by focusing computation on relevant parts of the system.
method: They introduce global and local algorithms that use dependency oracles to guide exploration and provide termination criteria, allowing customization and over-approximation.
result: The prototype implementation is competitive with and often outperforms specialized algorithms across diverse domains.
conclusion: The approach offers a flexible and principled way to trade precision for performance in fixed-point computation.

title: InterSAGE: The Secure And Verifiable Interoperability Protocol For An Internet Of Agents
authors: Zhenhua Zou, Sheng Guo, Qiuyang Zhan, Lepeng Zhao, Shuo Li, Zhuotao Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emerging Internet of Agents enables LLM-powered agents to discover peers, invoke tools, and delegate tasks across organizational boundaries. Existing protocols increasingly define how agents exchange messages, but not how an agent proves its identity, authorization, advertised capabilities, or accountability after delegation. We present InterSAGE, a trust-native protocol suite that supplies this missing security substrate alongside, rather than in place of, communication protocols. InterSAGE comprises four layers: Persistent Identity, Discovery, Trust Negotiation, and Accountability. Its four core primitives are: (1) Agent Identity Cards that bind developer, code package, operator, and deployment context; (2) capability-aware discovery using DID-bound Verifiable Credential manifests; (3) trust negotiation combining monotonic capability attenuation with two-tier access control; and (4) kernel-mediated cryptographic audit trails that bind usage, delegation, and execution traces to agent identity without a consensus ledger. InterSAGE is designed to complement MCP, A2A, ANP, and AG-UI, allowing communication protocols to evolve independently while keeping trust semantics explicit, portable, and verifiable. We compare InterSAGE with more than 50 efforts spanning agent protocols, decentralized identity, OAuth/OIDC extensions, zero-trust governance, delegation, and audit architectures. We show that no prior architecture jointly enforces persistent identity, capability-aware discovery, trust negotiation, and accountability as a unified four-layer trust substrate for secure agent interoperability.
tldr: InterSAGE is a protocol suite for secure and verifiable interoperability of LLM-powered agents, focusing on identity, authorization, and accountability.
motivation: Existing agent communication protocols lack mechanisms for proving identity, authorization, and accountability across organizational boundaries.
method: InterSAGE introduces four layers (Persistent Identity, Discovery, Trust Negotiation, Accountability) and four core primitives including Agent Identity Cards, capability-aware discovery, trust negotiation, and kernel-mediated audit trails.
result: The paper compares InterSAGE with over 50 efforts and claims no prior architecture jointly enforces all four trust layers.
conclusion: InterSAGE provides a trust-native substrate that complements existing communication protocols, enhancing security and verifiability in agent interoperability.

title: ProbSplat: Efficient Probabilistic Hardware For Gaussian Splatting In 3d Scene Reconstruction
authors: Siddarth Gottumukkula, M P Samartha, Vedant Pahariya, Priyanshi Jain, Amit Ranjan Trivedi, Priyesh Shukla
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents ProbSplat, a Compute-in-Memory (CIM)-inspired architecture based on programmable and energy efficient floating-gate inverter columns for probabilistic computing. Improving upon our prior work, ProbSplat programs and stores both means and variances of Gaussian mixture components, and evaluates log-likelihood for gaussian splatting during scene reconstruction with high energy efficiency, suitable for robotics and augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR) at the edge. Our proposed scheme enables independent control of both mean and variance via deterministic adjustment of floating-gate MOSFET threshold voltages, increasing the fidelity of hardware to program probability distributions. The design is simulated in 180nm CMOS on 1.8 V at 50 MHz and achieves mean-variance independence with <2.4% deviation during 3-D Gaussian mixture modeling. Compared to conventional digital implementations, ProbSplat significantly reduces compute complexity, memory footprint, and power consumption. The scalable framework consumes 18pJ energy per log-likelihood inference with 4-bit precision while operating for 500 mixture functions in a 3-D GMM. Scene reconstruction with ProbSplat's characteristics gave satisfactory fidelity of 21.99 PSNR (dB) at 8-bit precision.
tldr: ProbSplat is a compute-in-memory hardware architecture for probabilistic Gaussian splatting in 3D scene reconstruction, focusing on energy-efficient edge computing.
motivation: The paper aims to enable efficient 3D scene reconstruction for robotics and AR/VR at the edge by reducing compute complexity, memory footprint, and power consumption.
method: The authors design a CIM-inspired architecture using programmable floating-gate inverter columns to store and evaluate Gaussian mixture components, with independent control of means and variances via threshold voltage adjustment.
result: Simulated in 180nm CMOS, the design achieves <2.4% deviation in mean-variance independence, consumes 18pJ per log-likelihood inference, and yields 21.99 PSNR for scene reconstruction.
conclusion: ProbSplat demonstrates a scalable and energy-efficient hardware solution for probabilistic computing in 3D scene reconstruction, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Completeness And Incompleteness Of Basic Matching Logic
authors: Grigore Rosu Xiaohong Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Basic matching logic is matching logic without definedness. Symbols are interpreted as set-valued operations, element variables denote singletons and are bound by [MATH], and no connective uniformly internalizes totality. For basic matching logic without fixpoints over an arbitrary one-sorted finitary signature, we prove ([MATH] iff [MATH], for arbitrary, possibly infinite [MATH]) and, as a corollary, conservativity of the definedness extension. The proof localizes [MATH] to a theory [MATH] and reduces semantic consequence and derivability to the same local relation: [MATH] iff [MATH] iff [MATH]. A double-cover construction establishes the semantic equivalence. Least fixpoints destroy effective axiomatizability. Over a signature with one unary and two binary symbols and no constants, validity is not recursively enumerable; hence no sound calculus with a recursively enumerable proof relation is even weakly complete, already for the empty theory and without definedness. The positive result is also sharp in the number of sorts. Global completeness fails with three sorts for a satisfiable [MATH]. Thus the completeness conjecture holds for one sort and fails in general. The negative results arise from sort flow, fixpoint effectivity, and, for hybrid logic, an obstruction to every well-founded calculus whose leaves are hypotheses or valid patterns and whose rules respect localization. This yields a matching-logic-independent dichotomy: the language with state variables bound by [MATH] and [MATH] over modalities of arbitrary arity is globally complete without nominals, while no calculus in that well-founded class is globally complete once nominals are added.
tldr: This paper studies completeness and incompleteness results for basic matching logic, a logical framework for program specification, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to settle the completeness conjecture for basic matching logic, which is relevant to formal verification and program reasoning, but not to the user's research areas.
method: They prove completeness for one-sorted signatures without fixpoints via a double-cover construction, and show incompleteness results for multi-sorted signatures and with fixpoints.
result: The paper establishes that basic matching logic is complete for one-sorted signatures without fixpoints, but incomplete in general, and that validity is not recursively enumerable in certain cases.
conclusion: The completeness conjecture holds only in restricted settings, and the negative results highlight limitations of the logic, but this has no bearing on quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On The Structure Of $(\min,+)$ Convolution
authors: Huanyi Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The [MATH] convolution is a central problem in fine-grained complexity, and whether it admits a truly subquadratic algorithm remains open. We study it through tropical polynomials, where [MATH] convolution is exactly polynomial multiplication. We introduce tropical decomposition width, a parameter measuring how finely a tropical polynomial can be decomposed into low-degree factors. We prove modular convexity theorems showing that bounded tropical decomposition width forces strong convexity on arithmetic subpolynomials. This yields deterministic algorithms for computing [MATH] in [MATH] time when the width is given, and in [MATH] time otherwise, without requiring a decomposition. For Multiple-Sequence [MATH] Convolution, we give a randomized algorithm running in [MATH] time for [MATH] sequences of length at most [MATH], improving the natural [MATH] bound. We also obtain conditional lower bounds, a faster single-entry algorithm, and new upper bounds for Multiple-Choice Knapsack. Finally, bounded-decomposition-width classes admit interpolation algebras of finite generating rank, whereas distinguishing all tropical polynomials of degree at most [MATH] requires rank exactly [MATH]. We further show that tropical decomposition width cannot decrease under any flat [MATH]-algebra extension. These results connect efficient tropical multiplication with structural rigidity.

motivation: The (min,+) convolution is a central problem in fine-grained complexity, and the paper aims to understand its structure via tropical algebra.
method: The paper introduces tropical decomposition width, proves modular convexity theorems, and develops deterministic and randomized algorithms for computing (min,+) convolution under bounded width.
result: It provides algorithms with improved time bounds, conditional lower bounds, and results on interpolation algebras, connecting tropical multiplication with structural rigidity.
conclusion: The work contributes to theoretical computer science and tropical algebra, but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information and related areas.

title: Keep, Customize, Or Exit: Default Design And Token Pricing In Llm Reasoning Services
authors: Ahmet Bugra Gundogan, Yigit Turkmen, Melih Bastopcu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a large language model (LLM) service in which a provider chooses a per-token price and a default reasoning-token allocation, while a user may accept the default, customize the allocation, or exit. Larger allocations can improve accuracy but increase token cost and latency. We model this interaction as a Stackelberg game and derive the user's unique optimal customized allocation in closed form. For any price, the acceptable defaults form either an empty set or a compact interval. We characterize the provider's optimal default through a three-regime rule, reduce equilibrium computation to a one-dimensional price optimization, and prove the existence of the equilibrium. We further show that defaults affect the implemented reasoning allocation only when users value the convenience of avoiding customization; otherwise, every service-providing outcome implements the user's optimal customized allocation. Experiments with two compact open-weight reasoning models on five mathematics and science benchmarks support the accuracy-token model and show how model and task characteristics determine equilibrium prices, defaults, and reasoning allocations.
tldr: This paper models LLM reasoning services as a Stackelberg game, analyzing optimal pricing and default reasoning-token allocation.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how LLM providers should set prices and default reasoning allocations when users can customize or exit, balancing accuracy, cost, and latency.
method: They formulate a Stackelberg game, derive the user's optimal customization in closed form, characterize acceptable defaults, and reduce equilibrium computation to one-dimensional price optimization.
result: They prove equilibrium existence and show defaults only matter when users value convenience; experiments with open-weight models support the accuracy-token model.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for pricing and default design in LLM services, with practical implications for service providers.

title: A Dense Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm For Deciding Bounded-Cliquewidth Homomorphism Indistinguishability
authors: Radu Curticapean, Daniel Neuen, Amir Nikabadi, Tim Seppelt, Ben Young
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two graphs [MATH] and [MATH] are homomorphism indistinguishable over a graph class [MATH] if they admit the same number of homomorphisms from every graph in [MATH]. A wide range of relaxations of graph isomorphism arise this way: isomorphism itself over the class of all graphs [Lov\'asz, Acta Math. Hung. 1967], equivalence under the [MATH]-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm over the graphs of treewidth [MATH] [Dvo\'ak, J. Graph Theory 2010], and quantum isomorphism over planar graphs [Maninska-Roberson, FOCS 2020]. Since the class [MATH] is typically infinite, it is not clear a priori whether homomorphism indistinguishability over [MATH] is decidable; for planar graphs it is undecidable. Every class for which decidability was previously known is sparse. We give the first decidability results for dense graph classes: We introduce the dense Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm that decides homomorphism indistinguishability over the class of graphs of cliquewidth [MATH], the dense counterpart of treewidth. This relation was not previously known to be decidable. The algorithm colors [MATH]-tuples of vertex subsets rather than [MATH]-tuples of vertices. Beyond the class of all graphs of cliquewidth [MATH], we prove a general meta-theorem: homomorphism indistinguishability over every [MATH]-definable graph class of bounded cliquewidth is decidable, in randomized exponential time. For classes of bounded linear cliquewidth the bound improves to [MATH], and we show this is tight by exhibiting such a class for which the problem is [MATH]-complete. These are the first general algorithms for homomorphism indistinguishability over dense graph classes.
tldr: This paper introduces a dense Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm to decide homomorphism indistinguishability over graph classes of bounded cliquewidth, a purely graph-theoretic result with no connection to quantum information.
motivation: The authors aim to provide decidability results for homomorphism indistinguishability over dense graph classes, which was previously unknown. This is a fundamental question in graph theory and logic.
method: They define a dense Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm that colors tuples of vertex subsets instead of tuples of vertices, and prove a meta-theorem for MSO-definable graph classes of bounded cliquewidth.
result: They show that homomorphism indistinguishability over such classes is decidable in randomized exponential time, and for bounded linear cliquewidth the bound improves to coNP-complete.
conclusion: This work provides the first general algorithms for homomorphism indistinguishability over dense graph classes, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: TeleGapper: On The (un)reliability Of Privacy Policies In Telegram Mini Apps
authors: Luca Ferrari, Mariano Ceccato, Luca Verderame
abstract: ArXiv:2608.13390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Telegram Mini Apps are Web applications embedded within the Telegram client, forming an ecosystem of third-party services within one of the world's most widely used messaging platforms. Despite their growing adoption and access to Telegram-provided context, their privacy properties remain largely unexplored. Unlike ecosystems such as WeChat, which rely on tightly controlled, proprietary execution frameworks, Telegram adopts a different model: Mini Apps run inside a WebView, combining platform-provided context with standard Web capabilities and unrestricted outbound networking. This enables applications to transmit sensitive information to analytics, advertising, tracking, or other third parties through ordinary Web requests, often with limited visibility. Privacy disclosures are therefore critical for transparency. Telegram allows Mini Apps either to define an application-specific privacy policy or to rely on a platform-provided default policy. While the latter reduces the developer's disclosure burden, it may lead to generic statements that do not accurately capture actual data practices of individual Mini Apps. In this paper, we present TeleGapper, a black-box dynamic analysis framework to assess the privacy posture of Mini Apps by capturing runtime network traffic, identifying third-party communications, and comparing observed data flows against disclosed privacy information. We evaluate 278 working Mini Apps collected from tApps Center, a community-driven catalogue for discovering third-party applications in Telegram. We find that 59.4% contact at least one undisclosed third party, 78.8% rely exclusively on Telegram's default privacy policy, and none provides a consent or opt-out mechanism. These findings expose a substantial transparency and compliance gap in a widely used yet understudied ecosystem.
tldr: This paper analyzes privacy policy compliance in Telegram Mini Apps, finding widespread undisclosed third-party data sharing.
motivation: Telegram Mini Apps are widely used but their privacy properties are unexplored, and default policies may not reflect actual data practices.
method: The authors developed TeleGapper, a black-box dynamic analysis framework that captures network traffic and compares observed data flows with disclosed privacy policies.
result: Evaluation of 278 Mini Apps found 59.4% contact undisclosed third parties, 78.8% rely on default policy, and none offer consent or opt-out.
conclusion: There is a significant transparency and compliance gap in the Telegram Mini App ecosystem.

title: Open Versioned Aggregates Of The Faa National Wildlife Strike Database (1990-2026): Conditional Damage Rates By Animal Family, Airframe, And Airport
authors: Denys Kolomiiets
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background. Aircraft-wildlife collisions are a documented aviation hazard. The FAA National Wildlife Strike Database is the main public source of U.S. reports, but raw extracts are large and rarely released as versioned aggregates. Methods. We convert the public FAA Access export (STRIKE_REPORTS) to SQLite, define a report as damaging when DAMAGE_LEVEL is one of M, M?, S, D, and fold rows into open aggregates (year, airport, species, aircraft, animal family) via hierarchical SPECIES_ID prefixes. We analyze all civil reports and a commercial subset (AC_MASS 3-5). Rates are per reported strike, not per flight hour, so every rate is conditional on a report having been filed. Trend statistics use complete incident years 1990-2025; cross-sectional facets cover the full seed, incident years 1990-2026. Results. Numbers are locked to the 2026-07-04 freeze. Reported strikes in 2025 reach a series high (24,458 total; 901 damaging). Species that dominate strike counts are not those with the highest damage rates: perching songbirds account for 41.1% of identified strikes but damage aircraft in 1.5% of reports (95% CI 1.4-1.6), whereas deer account for 0.7% but damage aircraft in 81.8% of reports (95% CI 79.8-83.7). Airports ranked by total strikes (led by Denver Intl) diverge from rankings by damaging strikes (led by Sacramento Intl); across the 452 airports with at least 50 reports, volume and conditional damage rate are negatively rank-correlated (Spearman rho = -0.44, p < 0.001); large stations plausibly capture minor events more completely, so this is not a hazard ranking. The share of reports labeled damaging declines over decades, consistent with improved reporting of minor events, while absolute damaging counts peak in 2025. Conclusions. Versioned open aggregates and a documented damage-rate analysis enable independent reuse; released under CC BY 4.0.
tldr: This paper analyzes the FAA National Wildlife Strike Database, providing versioned aggregates and conditional damage rates by animal family, airframe, and airport.
motivation: The authors aim to make the FAA wildlife strike data more accessible and to provide a documented analysis of damage rates, which is useful for aviation safety but not related to quantum information.
method: They convert the FAA Access export to SQLite, define damaging reports based on damage levels, and aggregate by year, airport, species, aircraft, and animal family. They compute conditional damage rates and analyze trends.
result: They find that species with high strike counts (e.g., songbirds) have low damage rates, while deer have high damage rates. Airport rankings differ by total vs. damaging strikes, and there is a negative correlation between volume and damage rate.
conclusion: The paper provides open, versioned aggregates and a damage-rate analysis, but it is entirely unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Limits On Velocity Recovery From The Pursue Sensor Videos
authors: Ravi Kopparapu Jacob Haqq-Misra
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper analyzes the 112 sensor videos released by the U.S. Department of War under the PURSUE (Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters) initiative. Redactions to the on-screen displays limit the information available for identifying the nature of the reported unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP). The rate at which any object transits across part or all of a frame can be measured in pixels per frame; however, converting this to a physical velocity also requires (1) the range to the object, (2) the velocity of the observing aircraft, (3) the aspect angle between the object's path and the observer, and (4) the field angle of the camera sensor. No sensor video in the PURSUE corpus provides this complete set of information. In one clip (DOW-UAP-PR113), the object crosses visible depression-angle markings, allowing the camera's field of view to be reconstructed. Even this clip does not provide sufficient information to distinguish between a bird flying past the sensor at close range and a large craft traveling at Mach 5 a kilometer away. A second clip (DOW-UAP-PR149) includes a vessel of known size in the frame, which can be used as a reference to calculate an upper bound of Mach 0.4 on the object's relative velocity. Without further information, the PURSUE sensor videos in their present form cannot fully resolve unidentified cases or conclusively indicate anomalous velocities.
tldr: This paper analyzes sensor videos of unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) to determine if velocity can be recovered, concluding that the videos lack sufficient information for conclusive velocity estimates.
motivation: The U.S. Department of War released sensor videos under the PURSUE initiative, and the authors aim to assess whether these videos can resolve the nature of UAP by estimating object velocities.
method: The authors examine 112 sensor videos, focusing on two clips: one with depression-angle markings to reconstruct field of view, and another with a known-size vessel as a reference. They analyze pixel-per-frame motion and consider required parameters like range, observer velocity, aspect angle, and field angle.
result: Most videos lack complete information for velocity conversion. In one clip, the field of view could be reconstructed but still cannot distinguish between a close bird and a distant fast craft. In another, a known-size reference yields an upper bound of Mach 0.4 on relative velocity.
conclusion: The PURSUE videos in their current form cannot fully resolve unidentified cases or conclusively indicate anomalous velocities, highlighting the need for additional data.

title: Notes On Electrostatics In $\mathbb R^3$
authors: Vladimir Gol'dshtein, Wolfgang H. M\"uller, Reuven Segev
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A compact formulation of electrostatics is presented. Without using constitutive relations, including the aether relations, an expression for the potential energy of a charged region under a potential function is proposed, where the charge distribution is specified by the charge potential field. Assuming that during a virtual motion of the charge, the virtual work expended by the field is equal to minus the time derivative of the potential energy, an expression for the mechanical force functional is derived. The force functional contains the action of an asymmetric active stress field D_{i}E_{j}, the skew-symmetric part of which is the mechanical couple density.
tldr: This paper presents a compact formulation of electrostatics in R^3, deriving force functionals from potential energy without constitutive relations.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a general framework for electrostatics that avoids specific constitutive assumptions, potentially offering new insights into mechanical forces in charged regions.
method: They propose an expression for potential energy in terms of a charge potential field, then use a virtual work principle to derive a mechanical force functional involving an asymmetric stress field.
result: The derived force functional includes an asymmetric active stress term D_i E_j, whose skew-symmetric part corresponds to mechanical couple density.
conclusion: The work offers a novel theoretical formulation of electrostatics, but it is not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum systems.

title: Multi-point Variants Of The Newton-Raphson-Simpson Method Arising From Organizing A Formal Zero According To A Function $\phi$
authors: Mario Defranco
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fix an integer [MATH], and a function [MATH] with [MATH]. We define a multi-point variant of the Newton-Raphson-Simpson, which we call the max-phi method, as follows. We use [MATH] to define the iteration number of a rooted plane tree. Then we construct formal series that are weighted generating functions of rooted plane trees with iteration number at most [MATH]. Finally we use these formulas to define the max-phi method applied to an arbitrary [MATH]-differentiable function.
